name: Mark Twain
hook: Clemens, Hannibal and the Mississippi: the handful of facts behind every Twain clue.

facts.label: Samuel Langhorne Clemens
facts.statement: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Langhorne Clemens; under his real name he was born in Missouri in 1835.

facts.label: Hannibal, Missouri
facts.statement: Twain grew up in Hannibal, Missouri, on the Mississippi; its Boyhood Home & Museum and the Mark Twain Memorial Bridge honor him.

facts.label: Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn
facts.statement: Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn are his two Mississippi boyhood books; Huck is the "vulgar & bad" boy all the other children admire.

facts.label: The Prince and the Pauper
facts.statement: The Prince and the Pauper (1881) pairs Edward Tudor with Tom Canty and moves between London's poor and rich quarters.

facts.label: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
facts.statement: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court was illustrated by Daniel Beard, whose comic drawings shaped the book.

facts.label: Life on the Mississippi
facts.statement: Life on the Mississippi (1883) is his memoir of learning to pilot steamboats on the river, opening with Hernando de Soto.

facts.label: Hartford, Connecticut
facts.statement: Twain lived in Hartford's Nook Farm from 1871 to 1891, and his house there is now a museum.
